text: Efficient screening for Social Anxiety Disorder (SAD) requires valid and up-to-date instruments. The Social Phobia Inventory (SPIN) is a widely used and internationally validated measure. The German version has been validated in clinical and community samples, with a cut-off score of 25 established in 2008. However, changes in social interactions and communication patterns may influence responses to items, particularly in student populations. Moreover, the original German validation relied on DSM-IV criteria, and its validity under DSM-5 has not yet been sufficiently investigated. Given the increasing demand for brief screening tools, the Mini-SPIN offers a time-efficient alternative; however, its diagnostic accuracy in student populations has not been systematically examined.
source_label: Preliminary evaluation of the German SPIN and Mini-SPIN for screening social anxiety disorder in university students
